set.body:
TESTED, AND IT IS EXACT. Both out-of-core routes produce numbers identical to the in-memory path, not approximately equal:

  file_matrix_source, written as raw binary and read back
    contrast total vs in-memory        max|diff| = 0        IDENTICAL

  storage = 'block', out-of-core geometry with a disk-backed store
    contrast total vs in-memory        max|diff| = 0        IDENTICAL
    store created, 2 files, class reported as block_backed

Zero, not a tolerance. The out-of-core path is not an approximation of the in-memory path; it is the same computation with a different residency.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A TYPICAL VERIFIED-GOOD BEAD. 'Can I run this on a real brain without it falling over' is the single most common adoption question for any neuroimaging package, and it is the question the certification chain's scale work was built to answer. The answer here is good and it is provably good. A user cannot find that out.

  file_matrix_source   exported, appears in NO vignette and no runnable example
  storage = 'block'    an argument to geometry(), demonstrated nowhere
  storage_path         same

Both are on the list of 33 exports with no vignette presence recorded on bd-01KZYARD5697TRN2Q3S0E153BM. So the mechanism that answers the adoption question is invisible to the person asking it.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE PATTERN, and I think the pattern is now the most important structural finding of the review:

  1  bd-01KZYHGE7SAN8CB8YV4BFJ1CXQ   the unification claim - node effects and coupling really
                                     are blocks of one operator, verified to 2.22e-16 and with
                                     exact block decomposition. Never demonstrated.
  2  bd-01KZYBK55CR0T97SE36G9ESPNP   unequal-axis forms really do execute through
                                     measurement_form(left, right). The vignette shows hand
                                     arithmetic instead.
  3  this bead                        the out-of-core path is bitwise exact. No vignette,
                                     no example.

Every one is a genuine capability, verified by execution, that the documentation either omits or demonstrates in a way that conceals it. Taken together they say something sharper than any individual defect I have filed: THE DOCUMENTATION SYSTEMATICALLY UNDERSELLS THE PACKAGE. The gap is not that the docs are hard to read - though they are - it is that the three things most likely to win an adopter are the three things a reader cannot see.

PROPOSED, and it is cheap because nothing needs building: a short 'what this package can actually do' section or vignette carrying one runnable demonstration of each - the block decomposition with its exact numbers, an unequal-axis form through the engine, and a file-backed geometry agreeing with an in-memory one to zero. Three chunks. Every one of them already works today.
set.title: Verified: the out-of-core path is bitwise exact, and appears in no vignette or example
